newsitem.title: USA: Pickup driver crashed on CIA's doorstep.
newsitem.headline: Pickup driver crashed on CIA's doorstep.

text.p: A local man in a pickup truck sped through the main checkpoint outside the Central Intelligence Agency headquarters last month and crashed onto the CIA's front steps, the spy agency said on Wednesday.

In a stunning breach of security for an agency that spearheads U.S. anti-terrorism efforts worldwide, guards were unable to move quickly enough to activate pop-up metal barriers designed to halt intruders.

After racing past the checkpoint, the driver, identified as David Crump, 37, of McLean, Virginia, barelled through the sprawling CIA campus, careened across a grass square outside the headquarters building and began to climb its front steps before his pickup came to rest after hitting a handrail.
"It happened. We've learned from it and we're doing everything we can to prevent it from ever happening again," CIA spokesman Mark Mansfield said.
The incident occurred at about 8 p.m. on December 23 and had not previously been reported.

The CIA said the suspect, arrested by CIA security guards at the scene, had no known terrorist connections, criminal background or affiliation with the spy agency, nor was he armed at the time of the incident.

A U.S. official said Crump apparently was mentally disturbed and had been sent to a federal correctional facility for psychiatric evaluation. The local U.S. attorney's office did not immediately return a call seeking comment on the case.

The incident raised new doubts about physical security at the CIA. Security was strengthened with the addition of a guardhouse after a January 25, 1993, incident in which five people were shot, two fatally, while sitting in cars at a traffic light outside the turn-in to the sprawling campus.
U.S. law enforcement officials are still hunting for the alleged gunman in the 1993 shooting, a Pakistani national named Mir Aimal Kansi, reported to have fled to Pakistan, Iran or Afghanistan.
